newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers Squibb in research deal.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers Squibb in research deal.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co and Aurora Biosciences Corp said they made a collaborative research and licensing agreement with a potential value of more than $40 million.
Under the terms of the agreement, Bristol-Myers Squibb will obtain rights to use Aurora's fluorescent screening technology and will collaborate with Aurora to develop specific screening assays.

The two companies will also collaborate on the development of Aurora's proprietary ultra-high-throughput screening system targeted to screen 100,000 samples per day. When fully developed, the UHTSS will enable Bristol-Myers Squibb to substantially increase drug screening productivity and significantly reduce the cost of screening each compound.
Bristol-Myers Squibb will provide funding and license fees to develop and acquire the UHTSS and to use Aurora's fluorescent screening technology.

This funding, combined with potential milestone payments to Aurora associated with compounds identified from drug screens developed as part of the collaboration, could total up to $40 million. Further, if Bristol-Myers Squibb were to exercise its options for further screens, research funding and milestone payments could potentially generate additional revenues of up to $60 million. Aurora will also earn royalties on products identified from these screens.
